source_citation: Bourles, Gouriou and Chuchla (1999), On the circulation in the upper layer of the western equatorial Atlantic, JGR Oceans 104(C9), 21151–21170, doi:10.1029/1999JC900058.
layer: Subsurface eastward NEUC context. The central mooring study defines 65–270 m; historical western cores lie near sigma-theta 26.75 kg/m3. These different vertical definitions are not imposed as one uniform layer along the reference line.
sampling_context: Western sections in February 1993 and April 1996; central moorings June 2006–February 2008 and November 2009–January 2018 with 2002–2018 ship sections. Editorial section-to-section geography, not simultaneous observations or an annual/seasonal axis.

rejected_transport_width_transfers.reason: Chosen integration boundaries; not uniform paired current edges.
Reduced integration box underestimates NEUC transport; not full width.

excluded_inferences: No model 42 W–15 W integration span used as observed whole length.
No 35 W and 23 W records treated as a simultaneous trajectory.
No weak observed seasonal transport cycle converted to seasonal dimensional frames.
No filaments assigned invented eddy identities.
remaining_gates: Diagnose a compatible subsurface axis before asserting continuity across the separate section neighborhoods.
Resolve source recirculation, eastern filaments and termination before whole-current length.
Review historical two-degree latitude width with boundary and month-date precision support; no whole width or seasonal range inferred.
Keep mooring transport variability distinct from seasonal length/width geometry.

historical_width_evidence.layer_context: Velocity core near sigma-theta 26.75 kg/m3; not fixed-depth width at every level.
historical_width_evidence.remaining_issue: Independent extraction review, physical boundary diagnosis and repeated temporal support remain open; exact days unknown.
